parties: Prochant Healthcare, Inc. (US-based investee) v. Longshore Capital Partners (US-based PE investor)
headline: Prochant Healthcare secures strategic investment from Longshore Capital Partners; teams from ALMT Legal, SAM, Greenberg Traurig, McDermott advise on global and India legs.
sum: Prochant Healthcare, a Charlotte, North Carolina-based revenue cycle management services provider for home-based care, has received a strategic growth investment from Chicago-based Longshore Capital Partners. The transaction was structured with India-specific advice from ALMT Legal and SAM, while Greenberg Traurig and McDermott handled the global transaction.
implication: Multi-jurisdictional PE investment in a US-domiciled healthcare tech-enabled services business requires coordinated India-leg compliance (foreign investment policy, potential GST, labour, regulatory approvals) in tandem with US capital structure; use of separate India counsel signifies distinct regulatory requirements and entity structuring considerations for offshore PE funds.
detail: Prochant is a technology-enabled revenue cycle management services provider serving home medical equipment (HME), durable medical equipment (DME), infusion, and specialty pharmacy providers. Founded in 1999, the company operates with over 3,000 global employees and has been named to the Inc. 5000 list for six consecutive years. The investment will fund Prochant's advancement in AI, automation, technology and analytics capabilities, expansion of service capacity, and growth in core markets. Financial terms were not disclosed. The transaction appears to be a growth equity investment (not a full acquisition), with Prochant's management team retaining operational control.

framework.note: Controls inbound foreign direct investment by non-resident PE funds; governs repatriation of capital and profits by offshore investors; applicable to Prochant if receiving foreign capital directly or through India-domiciled vehicle.

framework.ref: Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) & Schedule 6 of FEMA Rules
framework.note: If Prochant structures any local entity or capital flow through a local co-investor or holding structure, controls on remittance of investment returns by non-residents.
Sectoral FDI caps and conditions for inbound investment in certain sectors; healthcare services may have specific conditions depending on whether it is classified as a permitted activity.
TDS obligations on royalties, management fees, dividends and interest paid to non-resident PE fund entities; withholding and reporting compliance.

framework.ref: Goods and Services Tax (GST) Act, 2017 – Sections 7, 94
framework.note: GST applicability on service fees charged by Prochant (RCM services are typically subject to GST); cross-border transaction treatment if offshore services are involved.
If Prochant or any investee entity is incorporated in India, compliance with equity issuance, related-party transaction reporting, and disclosure requirements.

framework.ref: Data Protection & Privacy: Information Technology Act, 2000 & Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
framework.note: Healthcare RCM services involve handling of patient/provider billing and reimbursement data; compliance with data localisation and cross-border transfer restrictions for sensitive health data.

framework.ref: Labour Laws: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947; Code on Industrial Relations, 2020
framework.note: If Prochant has operations or employees in India, compliance with labour and employment law, recognition of trade unions, layoff and retrenchment procedures in case of restructuring.

framework.ref: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Master Direction on External Commercial Borrowing (ECB), 2019 (if applicable)
framework.note: If the investment is structured as an offshore loan or hybrid debt-equity, compliance with ECB end-use restrictions and reporting to RBI's ECB portal.

structure.consideration: Not disclosed; structure is growth equity / minority stake investment to support scaling of Prochant's AI, automation, and service capacity.
conditions: Investment to be used for enhancing client experiences and outcomes
Advancement of technology, analytics, AI, and automation capabilities
Expansion of service capacity and operational scale
Development of additional revenue cycle management solutions for home-based care providers
Recruitment, development, and retention of talent
Pursuit of growth in core home-based care markets
approvals: Foreign investment approval under FEMA and FDI Policy (if applicable to Prochant's structure)
Board approval of Prochant Healthcare, Inc.
Potential RBI/FIPB approval (depending on structure and India entity involvement)
Internal approvals at Longshore Capital Partners
structure.novel: Structure preserves Prochant management team operational control and leadership; stated as 'partnership' to support organic growth and strategic acquisitions (implying minority equity stake with founder/management retained control). Use of separate India-leg counsel suggests bifurcated regulatory and compliance regime.

triggers.note: If investment flows through India entity or if Prochant has material India operations, foreign investment notification and reporting to FIPB/DPIIT required.

triggers.law: Income Tax Act, 1961 – Section 195 (TDS on payments to non-residents)
triggers.note: Any dividend, interest, management fees, or royalty payments by Prochant or India subsidiary to Longshore or offshore entities trigger 20% TDS (or lower treaty rate).
RCM services inherently involve cross-border processing of health/billing data; data localisation and cross-border transfer compliance critical if India operations exist.
RCM services supplied to India customers subject to 18% GST; if Prochant has a local entity or permanent establishment, GST registration and compliance mandatory.
